summary: Viva is an automated technical interview system built with Next.js and Mastra. It uses LLMs to ingest code repositories, generate project briefs, and conduct interactive interview sessions with candidates.

components.name: Interview Engine
components.purpose: Manages the logic for interview turns, question generation, and state transitions.

components.name: Agent Framework
components.purpose: Implements the interviewer agent using the Mastra framework to handle tools and memory.

components.name: Ingestion System
components.purpose: Handles reading and selecting files from various sources like GitHub or local directories.

components.name: LLM Utilities
components.purpose: Provides structured output generation and provider routing for different LLM backends.

components.name: Evaluation Suite
components.purpose: Scripts for benchmarking models and evaluating agent performance against scripted candidates.

decisions: Uses Mastra for agent orchestration and memory management.
Implements a state machine approach to manage interview flow in src/lib/interview/state.ts.
Supports both hosted LLMs and local Ollama endpoints via configuration in .env.
risks: Potential for model hallucination in file paths (mitigated by validation in eval/bench scripts).
Rate limiting risks when reading large repositories via GitHub API.
Complexity in maintaining structured output consistency across different LLM providers.

hooks.why: How are the 'friendly' vs 'tough' personas implemented and how do they influence the question generation?
Explain how the turn logic handles the transition between the agent-led rounds and fallback questions.
Why was the decision made to register agents centrally in the Mastra instance?
How robust is the system if the LLM fails to follow the Zod schema after multiple repair attempts?
What is the strategy for selecting which files to include in the prompt to avoid context window overflow?
How does this grounding check prevent the interviewer from hallucinating context from previous answers?
How does the app behave differently when LOCAL_MODE is set to true versus false?
How is the SQLite memory database managed across different deployment environments?
